title: Micro-latency investigation capture — Apr 08 2026
content:
Attendees: Avery, Marcus, Sofia, Eliot, Juniper

Purpose: capture today’s quick sync after the late-night smoketest surfaced repeated ~10–40ms micro-spikes at p99. These aren’t full stalls but create jitter visible in our latency SLO graphs for mixed-token workloads. Need to capture current hypotheses, test matrix we ran, and next experiments.

Observations (summary):
- Environment: dedicated staging pool (g5x2), model: open-llama-7B-quant, seq_len distribution: 32–1024 (mixed).
- Run: continuous mixed workload with simulated user patterns (50% short chat, 30% code-completion-ish, 20% long generative).
- Symptoms: baseline p50/p90 steady; p99 shows repeated spikes of 10–40ms lasting 1–3s windows, occurring ~5–8x per 10k requests.
- Traces: sampled traces show small GC-like pauses in host process in some cases; other traces show a short (~200–400us) kernel mismatch/queue-setup before token generation. KV cache hits correlate with fewer spikes.

Recent changes (possible contributors):
- Kernel selector greedy heuristic updated last Friday (PR 812) to prefer blocked matmul variant for LLA-type attention for performance reasons.
- Autoscaler prewarming ramp lowered to reduce costs — fewer warm worker slots for spiky traffic.
- Minor change in cache eviction TTL to free memory earlier for long-lived sessions.

Hypotheses:
1) Kernel selection regression: new heuristic picks a kernel that has lower throughput for short sequences under mixed workloads — queueing overhead shows up as micro-latency.
2) Prewarming reduction: fewer warm GPUs results in occasional cold-start micro-overheads when a burst routes to an un-warmed worker.
3) KV cache thrash: shorter TTL causing more KV recomputations for interleaved long-short session patterns.
4) Host-side scheduling: CPU-side thread pooling starvation when many async IO events coincide (observed in trace where syscalls spike).

Tests we ran during meeting:
- A/B run: old kernel-selector vs new (30m each) — old had 60% fewer micro-spikes. (Owner: Marcus)
- Prewarm bump: doubled prewarm for 1 hour on one pool — spikes reduced but not eliminated, p99 improved by ~8ms. (Owner: Sofia)
- KV TTL rollback: increased TTL from 30s back to 120s in a canary pool — noticeable drop in KV-related trace events. (Owner: Eliot)
- Threadpool metric capture: enabled fine-grained host CPU/thread metrics for upcoming 24h run. (Owner: Juniper)

Immediate action plan (next 72h):
- Roll back kernel-selector heuristic to previous version on a single canary region and monitor 12h window. (Marcus)
- Temporarily restore prewarm ramp to previous target for all staging pools to test impact on production-like bursts. (Sofia)
- Run long mixed-workload replay with TTL=120s for KV cache across three capacity classes (small/med/large) and capture trace diffs. (Eliot)
- Add sub-ms time-series for kernel queueing and per-request kernel-choice annotation to tracing pipeline. (Juniper)
- Add a small synthetic microburst workload (1000 concurrent tiny requests) to stress test threadpool behavior. (Avery)

Success criteria for rollback/mitigations:
- 24h p99 micro-spike frequency drops by >=50% in canary compared to baseline.
- End-to-end p99 improves by >=8–12ms for mixed workloads or shows stable reduction trend.

Risks and notes:
- Kernel rollback may reduce throughput for some long-seq heavy traces — need to watch cost/QoQ.
- Restoring prewarm increases reserved capacity cost; use short window for measurement.

Follow-ups / owners:
- Marcus: canary kernel rollback + 12h monitoring dashboard (due 2026-04-09 18:00 PT).
- Sofia: prewarm restore window + cost estimate and telemetry (due 2026-04-10).
- Eliot: KV TTL replay runs and trace diff artifacts (due 2026-04-10).
- Juniper: instrument kernel queue metrics + threadpool charts (due 2026-04-11).
- Avery: schedule cross-team postmortem if fixes don’t hit threshold after 72h (tentative 2026-04-13).

Open questions:
- Is the kernel selector change too aggressive for mixed workloads? If so, add sequence-length+workload-type feature into heuristic.
- Do we need an adaptive prewarm strategy keyed by recent QPS rather than static ramp?

Appendix (raw snippets):
- Example trace id: trace-20260408-8b42 — shows kernel-queue 320us + generation delta 18ms.
- Commands used for A/B: runtime/bin/run_bench --config mixed-small-large --kernel-selector=v2 --sample 10000
- Cost impact calc for prewarm bump: ~+$65/hr for staging pool (estimate).

Notes: this doc is a working capture. Will update after canary results and attach dashboards + diffed traces.
